messages:
mira: Heads-up — running into a weird issue when using the JS SDK inside our pnpm monorepo + edge builds. Works locally with node, but Vercel Edge build fails: 

mira: Error during build: 'Package "@redwood/sdk" has no export named "./runtime/edge"' even though that file exists and is referenced in package.json exports.

joel: hm. Are you using pnpm with symlinks? pnpm node_modules layout can cause bundlers to see the physical path, not the package root.

mira: yep pnpm@8, node-linker=isolated (default). workspace layout is standard, packages/ and apps/ in workspace. SDK is hoisted-ish via symlink.

sam: can you paste package.json exports for the SDK? sometimes missing explicit ./runtime path breaks ESM consumers.

mira: sure — here's the minimal relevant part:

```json
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
  "./runtime/edge": { "import": "./dist/esm/runtime/edge.js" }
}
```

mira: bundler (esbuild inside vercel) still resolves import to /path/to/.pnpm/____/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/esm/index.js and then tries to follow to ./runtime/edge relative to that file and fails?

tia: that rings a bell — when packages are symlinked, bundlers or node resolution can treat the symlink target differently. Two common fixes: 1) ensure the consumer imports the specifier exactly matching an export (import '@redwood/sdk/runtime/edge') or 2) configure pnpm to use a hoisted layout.

joel: also check the build-time resolver option: esbuild/webpack/rollup need to prefer package boundary exports. For esbuild we had to enable "conditions"/"exports" handling in our plugin. Vercel's internal builder might be older.

mira: tried exact import (import '@redwood/sdk/runtime/edge') — same error. Feels like the runtime/edge entry is not visible because pnpm symlinked package.json lives elsewhere?

alex: did you try setting "preserveSymlinks": true in Node or bundler? Node has a flag --preserve-symlinks, but many edge builders run in isolated envs. For webpack there's resolve.symlinks. For esbuild, there isn't a preserveSymlinks flag but you can resolve paths manually.

sam: quick repro I used locally: monorepo root -> apps/web -> app imports '@redwood/sdk/runtime/edge' -> build with esbuild -> fails when node_modules/@redwood/sdk is a symlink. When I ran pnpm install with node-linker=hoisted (pnpm v8+) the symlink goes away and build succeeds.

mira: ok trying node-linker=hoisted in .npmrc now. Any downsides?

joel: it can change hoisting semantics — watch out for duplicate installs and subtle platform differences. Another option: publish a small helper entrypoint that re-exports the runtime path from the top-level export, e.g., add "./runtime-edge": "./dist/esm/runtime/edge.js" so consumers can import '@redwood/sdk/runtime-edge' (single path) — not ideal but pragmatic.

tia: also consider adding a tiny file at package root: packages/sdk/runtime-edge.js that re-exports from ./dist/esm/runtime/edge.js. That avoids relying on exports resolution across symlinks. We did this in infra-sdk to avoid pnpm quirks.

mira: thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) is this worth a short DX note in the repo? 2) should our example Next/Edge sample app use the helper import to be more robust?

joel: yes to both. Add note: pnpm symlink issues + edge builders may not handle package exports paths — include workarounds: a) node-linker=hoisted b) small root-level proxy file c) ensure consumers import exact exported specifier.

sam: also add a troubleshooting snippet to devex docs with commands I used to reproduce:

```bash
# reproduce in a fresh workspace
pnpm i
cd apps/web
NODE_OPTIONS=--preserve-symlinks node -e "require('@redwood/sdk/dist/esm/index.js')"
# or build with esbuild to see error
pnpm --filter apps/web run build
```

mira: filed a tiny PR to the sample app to import '@redwood/sdk/runtime-edge' -> using a root proxy file for now. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/81 :eyes:

ci-bot: Built preview and ran edge build — all green. :white_check_mark:

alex: heads-up: for future, we should also test with turborepo and yarn workspaces. Each workspace manager has its own edge cases. Maybe add a CI job that runs the example app build with pnpm default and hoisted modes.

mira: good idea. I'll add a follow-up issue with checklist and link to this thread. thx all :pray:
